questions.stem: A train 150 meters long is running at a speed of 90 km/hr. How much time will it take to cross a railway signal pole?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: 
Step 1: Convert the speed from km/hr to m/s by multiplying by (5/18).
Speed = 90 * (5/18) = 5 * 5 = 25 m/s.
Step 2: To cross a stationary pole (which has negligible width), the train only needs to cover its own length.
Distance = 150 meters.
Step 3: Time = Distance / Speed
Time = 150 / 25 = 6 seconds.
DECOY BUSTING: If you forget to convert km/hr to m/s, you'll end up with a completely wrong number. Always check units.
EXAM INSIGHT: The (5/18) conversion factor comes from (1000 meters / 3600 seconds). Multiplying by (5/18) goes from km/hr to m/s. Multiplying by (18/5) goes the other way.

questions.stem: A train 200 meters long is running at 72 km/hr. How long will it take to cross a platform that is 300 meters long?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT:
Step 1: Convert speed to m/s. 
Speed = 72 * (5/18) = 4 * 5 = 20 m/s.
Step 2: To cross a platform, the train must cover its own length PLUS the length of the platform.
Total Distance = 200 (train) + 300 (platform) = 500 meters.
Step 3: Time = Total Distance / Speed
Time = 500 / 20 = 25 seconds.
DECOY BUSTING: 10 seconds is the time to cross a pole (200/20). 15 seconds is the time for a point to cross the platform (300/20). You MUST add the lengths together.
EXAM INSIGHT: Whether the object being crossed is a platform, a bridge, or a tunnel, always add its length to the train's length.
